The horizontal axis is labeled x and goes from 0 to 15, with marks at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. The vertical axis is labeled y and goes from 0 to 100, with marks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100. According to the surrounding text, x is hours spent studying and y is exam score, and the text gives a correlation coefficient of 0.69. There are 11 blue circular data points: about x=0, y=68; about x=1, y=70; about x=2, y=77; about x=3, y=79; about x=4, y=84; about x=5, y=86; about x=6, y=58; about x=7, y=89; about x=8, y=90; about x=9, y=95; and about x=10, y=96. A dark straight line of best fit is drawn across the plot, starting at about y=70 at x=0 and rising to about y=102 at x=15. Ten of the points form an upward trend close to the line, with higher x generally associated with higher y. One point at about x=6, y=58 lies well below the line and well below the overall cloud of points.
